one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event falls in the window: 3Q26 earnings on 2026-10-28 (IR events page). It is the last call for CFO Ken Parks; Claire McDonough joins as an advisor on 2026-11-01, after the window (8-K, Aug 2026). Orders are largely pre-announced. At Laguna on 2026-09-16 the CEO expected 'a very strong third quarter orders performance', put the $200B backlog 'very early in 2027', and said most of the 12 GW of new 2030-31 slots will be contracted in 4Q rather than 3Q. He also said data-center Electrification orders will run below the 1H pace of ~$2.5B a quarter. The risk is in the P&L. 2Q EPS of $2.47 missed ~$3.04 consensus. Aggregator consensus for 3Q is ~$4.07-4.15 EPS, which needs a large sequential step. The 2Q call guided 3Q Power margin to 17-18% (down from 18.8% in 2Q, the seasonal services low), Electrification margin modestly above 18.4% on $3.8-4.0B revenue, and Wind roughly break-even. The 10-Q shows 1H Wind EBITDA of -$657M against a ~-$400M FY guide, so 2H Wind must earn ~+$250M. That is the line most likely to slip or be re-guided. Positives in the window: 3Q buybacks ('the third quarter has given us another good opportunity'), Siemens Energy's record Gas Services orders, and steady hyperscaler capex. Negatives: the stock fell to ~$950 on 9/28-9/30 on 'smaller turbines / behind-the-meter' and AI-slowdown headlines before closing at $987 on 10/1. Net, I see no edge on direction. I use a near-symmetric lognormal, median ~$990 and sigma 14.5% (annual 52% / 3.5 = ~15%, trimmed slightly), with a small, roughly balanced earnings jump already inside that sigma.

fair_value.method: 60% forward P/E (2028E EPS ~$30 x 33x = ~$990, applied in Oct-2027) + 40% normalized FCF yield (2028E normalized FCF ~$8.0B at 3.25% = ~$246B, + ~$8B operating-adjusted net cash, / ~262M shares = ~$970). The blend is ~$985, about spot. That is down from $1,040 because post-Prolec D&A is higher and the FCF normalization is more conservative.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E revenue $57B x 19.5% adj EBITDA margin = ~$11.1B; less ~$1.5B D&A (PP&E ~$0.9B + intangibles ~$0.6B); less ~$0.2B excluded items; plus ~$0.35B net interest; 21% tax -> ~$7.7B net income / ~262M diluted shares = ~$29.4. Blended with consensus 2028E ~$30.5 -> $30; x 33x

inputs_detail.derivation: Management's 2028 outlook is $56B including Prolec (4Q25 release). I add ~$1B because the CEO at Laguna expects 2028 Prolec financials to be 'materially better' than projected, and 2026 revenue guidance went from $44-45B (Jan) to $45.5-46.5B (Jul).
Management targets 20% (Power 22%, Electrification 22%, Wind 6%). I trim 0.5pt for execution: 1H26 margin was 10.5% vs the 12-14% FY guide, and Wind lost $657M in 1H26 (10-Q segment note).

inputs_detail.value: Revenue $45.5-46.5B; adj EBITDA margin 12-14%; FCF $11.5-12.5B; Wind ~-$400M EBITDA

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q 1H26: PP&E depreciation $348M and intangible amortization $411M (up from $116M after the Prolec step-up), ~ $1.5B annualized. I hold ~$1.5B for 2028: PP&E depreciation rises with capex ($783M in 1H26) while purchase intangibles amortize down. Round 1 used ~$1.2B.

271M diluted weighted shares in 1H26 and 266.3M outstanding at Jun-30. $3B is left on the $10B authorization, and the CEO said 3Q26 gave 'another good opportunity' to buy. Net ~1.5% a year of reduction.

The 1H26 ETR of 10.5% is distorted by the nontaxable $3.99B Prolec remeasurement gain. The 2Q26 ETR was 29.8%, inflated by purchase-price-allocation updates and losses with no tax benefit. 1H25 was 22.6%. I normalize to ~21%.
Used only as a cross-check. My bottom-up $29.4 is close, so I use $30.

Spot is ~33x my 2028E and ~40-44x consensus 2027E. In Oct-2027, 2028 is the one-year-forward year, so the multiple compresses from ~42x to 33x as EPS growth slows from ~40% toward ~20-25%. What supports a premium: 2030 is mostly sold out and 2032 slots are already selling with cash down (Laguna), and peer Siemens Energy shows rising Gas Services margins and record orders. What caps it: the GLJ 2030-31 overcapacity argument (104-113 GW of capacity vs 88-90 GW of demand).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Normalized 2028E FCF ~$8.0B / 3.25% = ~$246B; + ~$8B net cash after treating part of the cash pile as customer deposits = ~$254B; / 262M shares = ~$970

inputs_detail.derivation: FY25 was $3.7B. With ~$12B in 2026, the target implies only >= ~$8B across 2027-28. It was set before the 2026 raise, so it is conservative, but it signals deposits partly normalizing.

~$7.7B net income + ~$1.5B D&A - ~$1.6B capex (1H26 annualized and rising) ~ $7.6B. I round up to $8.0B for continued modest deposit build: the CEO says the progress balance still grows more slowly than margin in backlog. Round 1 used $9.0B. I cut it because contract liabilities have already risen $14.1B in 1H26 to $39.9B, and the guide implies only ~$1.6-2.6B of 2H26 FCF.

$13.1B cash minus $2.8B long-term borrowings at Jun-30 = $10.3B. Adding 2H26 FCF (~$2B) less buybacks and dividends gives ~$10B at YE26. I haircut that to ~$8B because part of the cash is customer down payments ($39.9B of contract liabilities).
Between a premium electrical-equipment compounder (~3%) and a cyclical capital-goods discount (~4%+, the GLJ view). Unchanged from round 1.

bear.story: AI capex or data-center pushback (state moratoria, the 'smaller turbines / behind-the-meter' debate) slows slot conversion. Wind misses its 2H recovery. The market adopts GLJ's 2030-31 overcapacity frame and de-rates GEV to ~22x on ~$27 2028E EPS.

base.story: 3Q/4Q orders are strong and the backlog crosses $200B in early 2027. The January call shows 2026 Power margin-in-backlog change larger than 2025's low double digits. The 2026 guide is met, 2028 is reaffirmed or nudged up, and the stock trades ~34x a ~$30 2028E.

bull.story: The spring-2027 Capital Markets Day sets a 2030 framework well above the 2028 bridge: 30 GW/yr gas output, Electrification above $20B with MV-UPS and SST orders, and Wind profitable. 2028E EPS moves to ~$35-36 and the market pays ~40x.

thesis_break_reason: ~$640 (35% below spot, ~21x my $30 2028E EPS) is only consistent with the market pricing a broken 2028 outlook: slot reservations not converting to orders, margin in backlog going flat (Siemens or Mitsubishi capacity adds hitting price), or a material AI/data-center capex retrenchment. It is ~0.8 sigma below a ~$1,000 center at 43% annualized dispersion. My ladder puts ~19% probability below it, mostly from the fundamental bear branch rather than noise.

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI and data-center power demand: September AI-slowdown calls cut the stock 8.6% in a day, and state moratoria are live (NY enacted; Polymarket 18% for another state by year-end).

Whether gas turbine demand is secular or cyclical: GLJ sees 104-113 GW of 2030-31 capacity vs 88-90 GW of demand. Against that, 2032 slots are selling with cash down, and Siemens and Mitsubishi are both expanding capacity.
Margin ramp and EPS quality: 1H26 adj EBITDA margin was 10.5% vs the 12-14% guide, 2Q EPS missed, and post-Prolec amortization is ~$0.8B a year.
Wind: the 1H26 loss of $657M means 2H must earn ~+$250M to hit the ~-$400M guide; US onshore orders remain soft and Section 232 tariff clarity is pending.
FCF normalization: $39.9B of contract liabilities. 2026 FCF is deposit-driven, and the >= $24B 2025-28 cumulative target implies modest 2027-28 FCF.
CFO transition during a peak-execution period (Parks retiring; McDonough CFO from 2027-01-01).
reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with ~20 more searches and direct reads of primary documents (full 10-Q text from EDGAR, the company PDF transcripts of the 2Q26 call and Laguna, the Dec-2025 investor update, the Aug-2026 8-K, and the Siemens Energy Q3 FY26 release). The demand evidence held up or strengthened. Backlog is $176B ($88B equipment, $88B services), and gas under contract rose 100->116 GW (backlog 53 GW, SRAs 63 GW). 1H26 gas pricing was >20% above 4Q25, and 2H orders are guided to the high end of +10-20 points. 2032 slots are selling. Electrification equipment backlog is ~$45B, and data-center orders exceeded $5B in 1H26. A Capital Markets Day with a 2030 outlook is now set for spring 2027, inside my horizon. Peer Siemens Energy reported record Gas Services orders (+62%) with margin up 4pt, and hyperscaler 2027 capex consensus is near $1T. The new evidence that cuts the other way is mostly about earnings and cash quality. Post-Prolec intangible amortization (~$0.8B a year) and a ~21% normal tax rate put my bottom-up 2028E EPS at ~$29.4, not the $31 I had in round 1, close to consensus ~$30.5. Wind lost $657M in 1H26 against a ~$400M FY guide. 1H FCF of $9.9B against an $11.5-12.5B FY guide means 2H FCF of only ~$2B, so the deposit tailwind is fading. A CFO transition is under way. The fair value therefore falls from $1,040 to ~$985 (P/E $990, FCF yield $970), about spot. Sell-side consensus ($1,237 target, 30 of 37 Buy) is more bullish; I treat it as evidence of positive revisions, not as the answer. Ladder: a mixture of 85% lognormal (median $1,045, sigma 0.40) and 15% bear-branch lognormal (median $690, sigma 0.45). The overall median is ~$993 and dispersion ~43%, below the 52% realized vol because realized was inflated by the parabolic run and the September round-trip, but well above the 25-35% large-cap base rate. The scenario mean (25% $600 / 50% $1,030 / 25% $1,450) is ~$1,028, consistent with a slightly right-skewed ladder. Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were not used. Some sites (CNBC, GuruFocus, Business Standard) returned 403, so their facts are taken only where a second source agreed.
